name: description
label: Description
help_text: The final paragraph renders with emphasis styling to match the original design.
default:
Segmentation and Fabric is an identity-driven enforcement model. Policy is tied to who the user is and what the device is — not where it happens to connect. That policy is applied consistently across your environment: campus, branch, data center, and cloud.

R2 builds this on Cisco's Software-Defined Access (SDA) platform. SDA creates a centralized fabric where access intent is defined once and enforced everywhere. Configuration changes deploy consistently across sites. Unknown devices get classified. Policies do not drift because they are not maintained device by device.

This is not a product refresh. It is an operational shift — from a network your team manages manually to one that enforces policy automatically and reports on it clearly.

name: quote
label: Handwritten quote
help_text: The fallback shown when "Show Rich Text 2" below is OFF. Hidden here (and on the frontend) when "Show Rich Text 2" is ON.
default: "Authentication is the starting line, not the finish line. Every session inside the network needs to be classified, authorized, and enforced."

name: show_second_rich_text
label: Show Rich Text 2
help_text: Optional, OFF by default. OFF = show the Handwritten Quote below (default). ON = show Rich Text 2 (further down) in place of the Handwritten Quote, which is then hidden here and on the frontend. Mutually exclusive with Handwritten Quote — only one renders at a time.

name: rich_text_1
label: Rich Text 1
default:
Most segmentation programs don't fail at design. They fail in translation — between the policy your security team wrote and what switches, firewalls, and identity systems actually enforce. VLANs multiply, exceptions accumulate, and within a year nobody can say with confidence what can reach what.

That gap is invisible until an audit, an incident, or a lateral-movement finding makes it expensive. The strategy call exists to surface it early, while it's still a design conversation instead of a remediation project.

name: rich_text_2
label: Rich Text 2
help_text: Layout 2: shown when Columns above is set to 2 Columns. Layout 1: shown when "Show Rich Text 2" above is ON, in place of the Handwritten Quote.
default:
Fabric architectures like Cisco SDA close the gap by making intent the source of truth — policy defined once, enforced by identity, validated continuously. But the technology is the smaller half of the work. Readiness, sequencing, and operational fit decide whether it holds up.

That's what we assess on the call: where your environment is today, what a defensible target state looks like, and the shortest sequence between the two that your team can actually operate.

name: rich_text_2_as_quote
label: Display Second Rich Text as Quote
help_text: Renders Rich Text 2 using the same quote styling as the Handwritten Quote (vertical line + script typography), while keeping it a fully editable Rich Text field. Applies in both Layout 1 (when Show Rich Text 2 is ON) and Layout 2 (when Columns is set to 2 Columns).
